beats.say: Around 1914, a teenage Russian princess points a camera at a mirror.
beats.label: A SELFIE?

beats.say: Her camera is a Kodak Brownie. A box that cost one dollar.
beats.label: THE BROWNIE

beats.say: Its maker, George Eastman, had a promise.
beats.label: GEORGE EASTMAN

beats.say: You press the button, we do the rest.
beats.quote: You press the button, we do the rest.

beats.say: But his first Kodak, in 1888, cost twenty-five dollars. The Brownie, in 1900, cost one.
beats.label: THE PRICE

beats.say: A roll of film was fifteen cents, for six pictures.
beats.head: PRICE LIST, 1900

beats.say: Its name came from the Brownies, cartoon characters from popular children's books.
beats.label: THE BROWNIES

beats.say: About a quarter of a million of the first model were made.
Suddenly, anyone could take a snapshot.
beats.label: SNAPSHOTS

beats.say: The Brownie name lasted on Kodak cameras for about eighty years.
beats.label: 80 YEARS

beats.say: So the selfie is older than you think. It started with a one-dollar box.
beats.label: THE FIRST SELFIES
